record.paper_title: Some open problems concerning the convergence of positive series
record.original_question: Given an arbitrary series with positive terms, determine a general criterion or algorithm for deciding whether it converges or diverges. Is there any universal convergence test, or any structural pattern in convergence, for positive series?

evidence.quote: Problem 1. What decides if a positive series is convergent or divergent? Is there any universal convergence test? Is there any pattern in convergence?
Problem 2. Find an algorithm to determine whether a positive series is convergent or not.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} a_n$ denote an infinite series of positive real numbers $a_n > 0$. The series is said to converge if the sequence of partial sums $S_N = \sum_{n=1}^{N} a_n$ has a finite limit as $N 	o \infty$, and to diverge otherwise. Numerous classical tests are known for deciding convergence in special cases (comparison, ratio, root, integral, Raabe, Kummer, Bertrand, Gauss, condensation, etc.), but each test fails on suitably constructed examples.

Problem. Either:
(a) Exhibit a single "universal" convergence criterion, i.e. a property $P$ of the sequence $(a_n)_{n \ge 1}$ of positive terms such that $\sum_n a_n$ converges if and only if $(a_n)$ has property $P$, where $P$ is decidable/checkable for an arbitrary positive sequence; or
(b) Provide an effective algorithm which, on input a (suitably presented, e.g. computable) sequence of positive real numbers $(a_n)_{n \ge 1}$, decides in finite procedure whether the series $\sum_n a_n$ converges or diverges; or
(c) Prove rigorously that no such universal criterion or algorithm exists, and describe the structural obstruction to the existence of a universal test for convergence of positive series.
artifact.status_search_result: A classical theorem of Abel/du Bois-Reymond shows there is no universal comparison-type convergence test: for any positive divergent (resp. convergent) series one can find a positive series that diverges (resp. converges) strictly more slowly. From a computability standpoint, deciding convergence for arbitrary computable positive sequences is not algorithmically decidable. However, posed as the general informal question of a structural pattern or universal criterion, the problem remains open in the sense intended and is widely regarded as unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Abel's theorem on series (no universal convergence scale)
status_evidence.snippet: There is no most general convergence test for series of positive terms; for any positive divergent series there is another that diverges more slowly, and likewise for convergent series.
status_evidence.claim: It is classically known that no universal comparison scale exists, supporting that no fully universal test is known.
